content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 is involved in the metabolism of many drugs. Strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 can significantly increase systemic exposure to statins, thereby elevating the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration of such inhibitors is contraindicated. 2. Lovastatin can increase the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Nelfinavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed the approved monotherapy dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 4. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 5. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 6. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 7. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The maraviroc dose should be reduced to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of marijuana by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and marijuana can also increase nelfinavir levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of toxicity, and close monitoring is recommended. 11. Mitotane decreases the levels of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be required when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 12. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of modafinil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 13. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Close monitoring is required. 14. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of montelukast by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 15. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 17. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nateglinide by affecting insulin resistance. Hyperglycemia has been reported with protease inhibitors. Close monitoring is recommended. 18. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 20. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nintedanib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If adverse effects occur, therapy may need to be interrupted, the dose reduced, or discontinued. 21. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events with concomitant use. 22. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nitrenedipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 24. Nizatidine decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and norgestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised.
